subject: Private cluster node saturation causing p95 spikes — request for SLA review
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris@velvetcare.io>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: ops@velvetcare.io, lara@velvetcare.io
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: p95 jumps and 5xx rise on private cluster (on-prem)

Hi Mina,

We started seeing sustained p95 increases and a rising 5xx rate on our on-prem Redwood deployment around 03:40 PT this morning. The request queue on the primary inference nodes is stacking, and kernels are showing long scheduling latency; GPUs appear busy but the task scheduler isn't draining quickly. We've attached a short graph (p95) and a node queue dump.

Impact: customer-facing features are timing out intermittently (~10% of requests seeing 5xx/p50>1.5s; p95 pushed up to 4.2s). This is in our production VPC and has started affecting our daily batch jobs as well.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a config/regression on the runtime (kernel selection, batching) or an environmental issue on our nodes? We are subscribed to the standard SLA and need an expected ETA for mitigation and a plan for fallbacks.

Attachments: velvetcare_p95_2028-05-12.png (image), node-queue-dump-20280512.log (text), grafana-snapshot-2028-05-12.json (json)

Chris
Ops Lead, VelvetCare
ops@velvetcare.io

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris@velvetcare.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 jumps and 5xx rise on private cluster (on-prem)

Thanks Chris — really sorry you hit this. I'm on it and I want to get you an initial triage within the hour.

Quick asks so we can prioritize:
- Can you confirm whether this began after any config change or model swap?
- Are the node images on the latest infra bundle (we have a note in the Console when agents are behind)?
- Any recent traffic pattern changes (large batch, new endpoints) you can call out?

Next steps from us: I'll pull the runtime and batching telemetry immediately and ask infra to surface scheduler logs. Marissa, Vivek — can you join for a quick runbook? I'm escalating to infra and performance immediately.

Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 jumps and 5xx rise on private cluster (on-prem)

Adding context from the account side — VelvetCare is on a reserved Private plan with an SLA requiring p95 < 2s for inference routes in steady-state. If this persists past business hours tomorrow we'll need an executive-level update.

I recommend we:
1) Confirm whether this is a runtime regression (kernel selection, continuous batching throttle) vs. resource exhaustion (CPU pinning, nvlink saturation).
2) If resource exhaustion, propose a short-term mitigation: temporary autoscaling of GPU pool (burst/borrow capacity) or shift heavier routes to the fallback model variant (lighter quantized variant).
3) Communicate a concrete ETA to Chris and CPO Lara within 3 hours.

I can lead customer comms and procurement channel if we need SLA credits or temporary capacity. Mina — can you share triage notes ASAP so I can prep a short exec note?

-marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Chris Nolan <chris@velvetcare.io>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 jumps and 5xx rise on private cluster (on-prem)

Quick summary of what we've pulled so far (first-pass):
- Runtime telemetry shows a sudden increase in KV cache-miss ratio for the hottest routes starting 03:36 PT; this correlates with a surge of small requests with longer context lengths.
- Kernel selection logs indicate the runtime is falling back to a slower execution path for ~12% of tokens (we see a mix of FP16 -> fallback to unquantized path on a subset of layers).
- Node-level CPU steal is elevated on two machines (node-07 and node-11) in the primary pool — likely unrelated system process contention (we're requesting the box-level cron logs from the on-prem team).

Immediate mitigations we can push now:
- Toggle prefix/KV caching to aggressive on the affected routes (reduces repeated KV recompute).
- Force model variant to the 8-bit quantized variant for heavy routes to avoid the fallback path while we diagnose why kernel selection mismatched.
- If node CPU steal persists, recommend scheduling a maintenance window to clear background processes (we can orchestrate with VelvetCare ops).

I'll prepare a short playbook and a one-hour ETA for the customer. If the customer prefers, we can also enable temporary burst capacity from Redwood Dedicated pool (billing/approval required).

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

---
From: Chris Nolan <chris@velvetcare.io>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: lara@velvetcare.io, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 May 2028 22:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 jumps and 5xx rise on private cluster (on-prem)

Appreciate the quick response and the clear mitigation plan. We're happy to try the aggressive KV caching toggle and switch the hottest routes to the 8-bit variant — please let us know exactly which routes and configs you'll change so our on-prem ops can approve.

Also, two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm whether this pattern could cause any consistency or output-variance risks when moving from the primary model to the quantized variant (we have strict quality checks)?
- If we need to borrow Dedicated burst capacity, what's the expected time to spin up and the cost ballpark?

I'll attach a short failing request trace that shows the header and response for one 502; hope that helps. Lara (CPO) is on standby for exec updates if this goes beyond tomorrow.

Thanks,
Chris
Ops Lead, VelvetCare
